chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī ʿImrān, from Yūnus, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said:

I asked one of the two, peace be upon them, about the legal punishment of the mute, the deaf, and the blind. He said: “The prescribed punishments apply to them if they understand what they are doing.”

key_terms.الْحُدُودُ: the prescribed penal limits and punishments
key_terms.حَدِّ: the prescribed legal punishment in question

ai.seo_question: Do legal punishments apply to the mute, deaf, and blind in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith states that prescribed legal punishments apply to individuals with disabilities such as muteness, deafness, and blindness when they possess understanding of their actions. Its significance is that legal accountability is tied to comprehension and reason, not merely to physical condition.
